info.album: I Feel Fine / Long Tall Sally (A Tribute to the Beatles)

podcast.body: On October 18, 1964, while recording at Abbey Road Studios, the Beatles accidentally discovered the controlled feedback sound used at the beginning of this song. Paul McCartney plucked a bass string, and John Lennon laid his semi-acoustic Gibson guitar against Paul's bass amp, causing the guitar to pick up the bass note and feed back. Recognizing the cool sound, Paul and John asked producer George Martin to capture it, and it was subsequently edited into the track. This is considered one of the first uses of controlled or semi-controlled feedback on a rock record. "As far as anyone can tell, this was one of the first uses of control, semi-controlled, feedback on a rock record."

podcast.body: The Beatles produced promotional film clips for this song, along with others, as a means to appear on television without needing to perform live. This approach allowed them to reach a wider audience while avoiding the physical demands of constant touring and live TV appearances. "They also did this with I Feel Fine, Ticket to Ride, and Help."
